plan: In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This holds because if you bid above your value, you risk winning and paying more than your value, and if you bid below your value, you risk losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $3, I should bid exactly $3 to maximize expected profit, regardless of the beliefs or strategies of Betty and Charles.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy, regardless of what other bidders do. Bidding higher than value risks winning at a loss; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $24, I should bid exactly $24 to maximize expected profit, as this strategy is optimal regardless of competitors' behavior.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (winner pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding truthfully (bid = value) is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do—it maximizes expected profit since you win exactly when your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you never pay more than your value. Overbidding risks winning at a loss; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With my value at $11, I should bid $11 exactly.
